concept.name: Gas fee
concept.definition: A gas fee is the payment, denominated in the chain's native currency, that compensates the network for the computational resources a transaction consumes, priced per unit of 'gas' — the protocol's measure of computational effort.
concept.intuition: Gas is the meter on the world's shared computer: every operation you run ticks up a bill you must pay, whether or not the transaction succeeds.
concept.mechanics: Fee = gas units used × (base fee + priority fee). The base fee is set by the protocol per block (adjusting up to ±12.5% based on demand against a target block size) and is burned; the priority fee (tip) goes to the validator to incentivize inclusion. Users can cap total spend with maxFeePerGas, and unused gas is refunded.
concept.formula: gas fee = gas_used × (base_fee + priority_fee); e.g. 21,000 × (10 + 2) gwei = 252,000 gwei = 0.000252 ETH.
concept.failure_modes: Demand spikes can push fees above the value of small transactions, pricing users out; setting a gas limit too low causes the transaction to run out of gas, fail, and still consume the fee.
concept.misconceptions: Gas fees are not paid to a company — the base fee is burned and only the tip reaches the validator. A failed transaction still costs gas because computation was performed.
concept.example: Sending 1 ETH with a base fee of 10 gwei and a 2 gwei tip costs 21,000 × 12 gwei = 0.000252 ETH; the sender pays 1.000252 ETH total, the base fee of 0.00021 ETH is burned, and the validator keeps the 0.000042 ETH tip.

citations.source: Ethereum.org developer docs - Gas and fees
